tip: WIN — When the customer said "That's too much money" about the $8,500 repair, you didn't just accept it and move on—you reframed the entire value conversation. You explained why Sierra charges what it does: permits pulled by the city, proper electrical and gas work, warranty transfer to new owners. Then you asked the deciding question: "Is this a house you guys plan on keeping?" When they said they're selling very soon, you pivoted smoothly to replacement options with payment plans instead of fighting for a repair that wouldn't make sense for their timeline. That strategic listening and flexibility turned a potential walk-away into a scheduled specialist visit and genuine customer interest in exploring solutions.
